note: The hand-typed prompt supplied as the motivating example, expressed as bin selections and re-rendered canonically. Included as a fixture for the renderer: if the renderer cannot reproduce this, the vocabulary or the render rules are wrong.
source_prompt: Late Night Trap, 95 BPM, Heavy 808 Bass, Wet Synths, Female Background Vocals, Male Rap Vocals + Seductive Female Vocals, Dark Bedroom Production, Breathy Whispers, Slap Bass, Deep Sub Bass, Cinematic R&B Soundtrack West-Coast Feel
rendered_string: Trap, West-Coast Feel, Late Night, Heavy 808 Bass, Slap Bass, Deep Sub Bass, Wet Synths, Male Rap Vocals, Breathy Whispers, Female Background Vocals, Seductive Female Vocals, Dark Bedroom Production, Cinematic R&B Soundtrack

metadata._note: 95 BPM left the caption. See differences_from_source.

lyrics_provenance: This is the genuine paired example: the caption and lyrics both ship with the packaged ComfyUI audio_ace_step1_5_xl_turbo template, and the caption was the motivating example for this project. The lyric content is a joke at the template's own expense -- it describes building a ComfyUI node graph while the caption asks for late-night trap.
checker_findings: Caption and lyrics describe different things: the caption is late-night trap/R&B with seductive backing vocals, the lyrics are a technical walkthrough of node graphs. That mismatch is the template's joke, and it is also the exact failure mode the caption/lyric consistency rules exist to catch, which makes this pair a good regression fixture rather than a bad example.
No blank line between sections. The model's guide explicitly asks for blank-line separation so section boundaries are unambiguous; the checker raises four warnings.

Verse lines run 11-13 syllables, above the model's recommended 6-10 band; the chorus and outro sit at 7-10 and are inside it. The counts are at least consistent within a verse (11,11,13,11 and 11,11,11,11), so lines in the same position agree within the guide's +-2 tolerance.

No section modifier anywhere, and no performance, vocal or energy tags. All performance direction is left to the caption, which is a legitimate choice but means several caption selections (Male Rap Vocals, Seductive Female Vocals, Breathy Whispers) have no counterpart in the lyrics for the consistency check to compare against.

Heavy technical jargon -- KSampler, VAE, CFG, ControlNet, Lora, ComfyUI -- produces hard phoneme sequences, and the guide warns that the model drops or slurs consonant clusters. This is precisely the content that most needs the independent ASR the design currently marks unverified.

Rhyme detection is spelling-based and approximate: it found the scheme in Verse 1 (AABB) and the Outro (AABB) but missed three genuine rhymes (queue/through, height/right, chain/insane). That is a concrete argument for the pronunciation lexicon the design already names as the real implementation of this gate.
differences_from_source: **95 BPM was moved out of the caption and into metadata.bpm.** The source prompt has it as a tag; ACE-Step's own tutorial says not to do that: 'Don't write tempo, BPM, key, and other metadata information in Caption. These should be set through dedicated metadata parameters (bpm, keyscale, timesignature, etc.)'. A redundant number in the caption is at best noise and at worst a conflict when the two disagree.
Order is canonical (bins in render_order) rather than the order they were typed in. Same content, stable bytes.
'Late Night Trap' was split into the genre 'Trap' and the scene 'Late Night', so that either can be changed without touching the other.
'Cinematic R&B Soundtrack' is carried by one vibe_reference option rather than being composed from a genre and a fusion, because the compound phrase is what reads naturally in a tag prompt.
'West-Coast Feel' moved next to the genre instead of trailing the list; the model reads tag order loosely, but a fixed order is what makes the prompt hash stable.
13 tags against a budget of 14, so nothing was dropped.
